Coordinates and river km from PEGELONLINE station metadata (km 55.63, agency STANDORT DRESDEN).

measurement_history.fact: Start of readings and early reading hour: not found. The hyd1d record used here starts 1960-01-01.

A 1996 federal study charts 140 years of falling levels at Dresden. The fall was fastest around 1890 to 1904 at most gauges from Dresden to Magdeburg (about 3 cm a year). After low-water works shortly after 1934, the bed near Dresden appears to have held about steady. Work on the Augustus Bridge, where the gauge sits, may have affected readings directly.
The gauge is at the Augustus Bridge and is read automatically by the federal waterway agency.
Neighbor comparison (hyd1d_stepscan.py) found no gauge-zero step.

public_notes: The level is measured against a fixed mark, not the riverbed, so it is not the water depth. A 1996 federal study found the Elbe bed near Dresden wore down fastest around 1890 to 1904 and has changed little since the 1930s. Values from 2026 are unchecked raw readings, and August 11 to September 14, 2026 is missing.
